annotations.title: Where has a size like mine actually cleared (paid)

description: YOU HAVE A SIZE AND YOU WANT TO KNOW WHERE IT HAS ACTUALLY CLEARED. Every other exit reading here is about one vault; this asks the same question across every vault whose withdrawal history we have read, which is the question an allocator with capital actually has. Send `amountUsd` and each vault comes back with one of THREE verdicts, and the middle one is the finding: `paid-in-one` means a single settled withdrawal at least that large has been recorded there; `paid-across-a-day` means that much has left in one day and never in one withdrawal, which is a different fact and not a weaker version of the first; `never-asked-this-size` means nothing that large has been withdrawn, which is NOT a refusal and NOT a failure, because most vaults have never been asked. It exists because an auditor screened a $6M exit from a vault declaring $15.10M withdrawable, got a supporting answer, and found the largest withdrawal ever observed there was $500K. Declared liquidity is a LEVEL at an instant; what has left is a FLOW; only the second is evidence about a size. The two are never divided by one another and no ratio between them is returned. `population` names how many vaults have no history at all, because those are UNREAD rather than untested and must not be counted as either answer. Nothing here is a forecast: a vault that paid this much last March can refuse today. PAID.

amountUsd.description: The size you are weighing, in US dollars, e.g. 6000000. Required: "can I get out" has no answer without one.

limit.description: How many vaults to list, 1 to 100. The counts cover the whole population either way.

name: exit_screen

amountUsd.description: The size asked about, read back.

cannotSee.description: What a record of settled withdrawals structurally cannot contain.

counts.description: How many vaults fall in each of the three verdicts, over the whole population rather than over the listed rows.

limits.description: Why this is a record and not a forecast.

meta.description: How current this answer is and what it was read from: `freshness` and the ages behind it. Present on every answer from this server, whatever the tool.

population.description: `withHistory` and `withoutHistory`: a vault with no withdrawal history is unread, never a vault nobody has withdrawn from.

vaults.description: Each vault with its verdict, its largest single exit and when, its busiest day, how many withdrawals we have seen and how far back the history reaches.

verdicts.description: What each verdict means, beside the answer rather than in documentation you have to find.

warnings.description: Anything the server wants a caller to know about THIS answer before acting on it. Empty is the normal case and is not a guarantee.
